note.question: What role does energy stacking play in battery energy storage systems?
note.overview: Despite the great potential benefits of battery energy storage systems (BESSs) to electrical grids, most standalone uses of BESS are not economical due to batteries’ high upfront costs and limited lifespans. Energy stacking, a strategy of providing two or more services with a single BESS, has been of great interest to improve profitability. However, some key questions, for example, the underlying mechanism by which stacking works or why and how much it may improve profitability, remain unanswered in the literature.

Without a power constraint, we always prefer equal excess (Lemma 1); however, if the power capacity limits the amount of regulation provided in the high-price period, then Lemma 2 suggests choosing x∗ L > x∗ H to take advantage of the remaining power in the low-price period.

Although most key properties of the base model hold when power P is sufficiently large but still binding (e.g., A∗ stk > A∗ arb and R∗ stk > R∗ reg; see Table C.1 for details), it is worthwhile to mention some consequences of the constraint.
